extracted.intended_audience: historians/ethnographers and researchers estimating historical aboriginal populations (California valley/delta region)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and methods for estimating pre-contact and early-colonial aboriginal population sizes in California river/delta regions using mission records, explorers' diaries, area/stream-density comparisons, and other documentary sources. Emphasizes combining multiple approaches and adjusting for regional contact histories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of mission baptism records (baptism factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use mission baptism totals as a documentary baseline and convert them to aboriginal population estimates via a 'baptism factor' (the author previously 'doubles the baptism number' as one procedure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The baptism factor is arbitrary and must be adjusted by local conditions: author uses doubling in some earlier instances (50%), but finds this inappropriate for some groups (e.g., Cosumnes where baptisms represented ~19.2%). Examples in text: delta tribes ~50% baptisms, Cosumnes ~19.2%, Mokelumne-group assumptions between 7% and 20% depending on resistance to missionization. Do not apply a single universal multiplier without regional justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group comparison / average group-size method
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate population by applying an average population size derived from comparable tribal groups (the author computed an average of ~705 for nine groups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If enough comparable groups exist, use their mean to infer populations for poorly-documented groups. Adjust the average for tribes known to be unusually large or small (author adjusted Moquelumnes upward because multiple sources indicate they were larger-than-average).

rubrics_metrics.name: Area comparisons / density per square mile
rubrics_metrics.description: Project tribal territories on a map, compute area (square miles), and apply an estimated population density (persons per square mile) to obtain totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used where interfluvial hinterland is inhabitable and area comparisons are meaningful. The author computed area and density (e.g., area 775 sq mi with population 3,400 gives density 4.39 persons/sq mi) to infer populations. Choose densities based on analogous areas or other methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linear stream-density comparisons (villages per river mile)
rubrics_metrics.description: When populations are concentrated along stream banks, compare village counts or villages-per-linear-mile between similar rivers to estimate population on the target river.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author compares Cosumnes and Mokelumne stretches (24 miles vs 22 miles) and assumes similar villages-per-mile to infer number of villages and multiply by assumed persons per village (e.g., 300). Use linear comparisons only when rivers are ecologically similar and human settlement is riverine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of explorers' diaries and observer counts (houses, warriors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use first-hand accounts (diaries of Viader, Abella, Duran, etc.) reporting numbers of houses, warriors, or qualitative descriptions ('he saw 200 warriors', 'village had 60 houses') to infer population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infer persons per house (e.g., suggestion that a huge house could accommodate 9 persons; author estimated village sizes from house counts and circumferences) and combine with counts of houses/villages. Treat single-visit counts as snapshots that may under- or overestimate total local population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of contemporary/pioneer censuses and later estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate later censuses or pioneer accounts (e.g., Gatten's 1846 enumerations, Savage, F. T. Gilbert) as checks or extrapolations to pre-contact numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These sources may be exaggerated or reflect post-epidemic attrition; the author sometimes halves pioneer figures as a conservative adjustment. Use them as one input among several, not as sole evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use military/auxiliary counts to infer total population
rubrics_metrics.description: When records give counts of fighting auxiliaries (e.g., '450 Gentiles auxiliares'), use demographic assumptions about the army composition to back-calculate total population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author assumes such armies included at most half the males over age ten, a unity sex ratio, and children ~15% of population to convert an auxiliary count into an implied total. Make explicit demographic assumptions when using this method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for displacement, migration, extermination, and missionization
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust population inferences for demographic and spatial shifts caused by Spanish military pressure, missionization, forced removals, migrations upstream/out of area, or local extermination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author repeatedly notes that baptisms undercount survivors due to escape/migration; evidence that tribes 'retired across the estuary' or were 'pushed north' implies mission records may miss relocated subpopulations. Consider historical narrative about movement and attrition when interpreting documentary counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine multiple independent methods and take the mean
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce several independent estimates (e.g., by stream comparisons, baptism data, adjusted tribal averages, extrapolation from pioneer accounts) and use their average as the best estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author lists three or four methods for a group (e.g., Moquelumne: 7,200; 4,800; 4,870; 6,000) and adopts the mean (5,720). Use multiple methods because each has different biases; averaging reduces method-specific error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust baptism factor regionally according to contact intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that the proportion of a group's members baptized varied regionally with proximity to missions, resistance to missionization, and timing of contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author gives examples: heavily missionized delta tribes may show ~50% baptisms; Cosumnes group lower (~19.2%); Moquelumne tribe resisted and author uses a smaller baptism percentage (e.g., 7% for Moquelumnes). Select baptism multipliers based on local historical evidence of mission contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid false precision; round estimates and flag insignificant digits
rubrics_metrics.description: 'No significance should be attributed to the third and probably also the second digit in these numbers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report rounded numbers and explicitly acknowledge uncertainty; do not imply unwarranted precision in population estimates derived from fragmentary sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Village-count method with assumed persons-per-village
rubrics_metrics.description: Use enumerations of villages (e.g., Merriam's list of villages) and assign an assumed persons-per-village (range provided, e.g., 200–400, or values from analogous battle reports like 475) to compute totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author uses different assumed village sizes for upper/lower stretches (e.g., lower villages possibly 475 each, others 300 or 250 depending on region), drawing on analogous reports (Moraga, Soto) to calibrate per-village estimates. Justify chosen per-village number with comparable local evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of spatial unit: stream length vs area depending on landscape
rubrics_metrics.description: Select linear stream-measures when populations concentrated on banks of similar rivers; use areal measures when territory is a marsh/interlaced with sloughs where linear comparisons fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author states linear distances are useful where rivers are similar ecologically and human population concentrated along banks; 'Where a territory is marked by a network of creeks and sloughs ... areas must be substituted.' Choose the spatial unit that matches settlement ecology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map-based territorial delineation using ethnographic/cartographic sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Delineate probable tribal territory boundaries using ethnographers' maps (e.g., Schenck) and then apply area or stream-density methods within those boundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author follows Schenck's map where possible but also critiques and refines it (e.g., restricting alleged tribe distributions). Use maps critically and revise boundaries when documentary evidence suggests errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize name variants, record confusion, and treat counts cautiously
rubrics_metrics.description: Beware of multiple name variants for the same group in mission books and later sources (e.g., Siakumne, Ssicomne, Zicomne etc.), which can produce duplicate or fragmented counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons and aggregations across records require careful cross-referencing of name variants; apparent disparities (e.g., low baptisms in one mission but presence in others) may reflect naming confusion rather than absence.
